role.altitude: The HR Administrator stops keying and chasing records and becomes the owner of HR data quality and the AFAS, Recruitee and Studytube workflows that move the data: they write the rules, review exceptions, keep test cases and audit samples, and fix the process when a mutation goes wrong.
reach: Pre-checking payroll mutations (new hires, leavers, changes in hours and scale) before the Payroll Specialist's month close
Checking flex worker hours and agency invoices against orders for the Bookkeepers
Tracking certificate expiry (forklift, VCA, food safety) and enrolments for L&D
The admin from offer to start that Recruiters now hand off by email
Data quality checks and fixes for the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst's Power BI dashboards
Keeping contract history and records in order for HR Business Partners (ketenregeling, aanzegplicht dates)
role.ceiling_note: About 40 to 55% of the roughly 3,200 hours a year across 2 FTE can be freed. The limits are legal duties that need a person (the in-person ID check for loonheffingen and WAV, signing contracts), AVG limits on medical and absence data under Wet verbetering poortwachter, EU AI Act high-risk rules for candidate screening, works council consent (WOR art. 27) for new systems that process employee data, and how clean the AFAS master data is today.
skills_to_grow: Configuring AFAS Profit workflows and connectors, and Power Automate
Writing validation rules and test cases for document extraction and HR mutations
Practical AVG/GDPR and EU AI Act knowledge for HR data (retention periods, special category data, high-risk use)
Process mapping and exception handling: owning a queue, not a task list
Reading Power BI data quality reports and doing root-cause fixes
Writing clear policy answers in plain Dutch and English for a chatbot knowledge base
role.ambitious_version: Every employee and flex worker on all three sites has a complete, correct and current file, with contract, ID/WAV check, certificates, leave and CAO scale all checked every night. Each month starts with zero open payroll mutations, contract end dates and certificate expiry are never missed, and staff get answers to HR questions in their own language within minutes. The two administrators run this as a monitored system, report error rates to the HR Director and take on flex-pool administration and payroll pre-checks.

tasks.short: File and check personnel documents in AFAS: contracts, certificates, leave forms, appraisals, grievances.

today.trigger: A document arrives by Outlook, Teams, paper from a site office, or a manager's request
steps: Open the email or scan and work out the document type and the employee
Check it for completeness (signatures, dates, matching personnel number)
Enter key fields in AFAS Profit and upload the file to the employee dossier
Chase what is missing and track it in an Excel list
File restricted documents (grievances, appraisals) with the right access
drudgery: Renaming and dragging PDFs into the right dossier folder
Retyping dates and names from scans
Keeping the Excel list of missing documents up to date
today.time_sinks: Paper from the Tilburg and Venlo site offices, unsigned or incomplete forms, and working out which employee or flex worker a document belongs to.

lenses.faster: Incoming documents are classified, matched to the employee, and their key fields read out automatically, so the administrator only checks a prepared entry instead of opening, renaming and typing.
lenses.autonomous: A shared HR mailbox and upload form trigger the flow. Complete standard documents are filed in AFAS without a touch, and incomplete ones trigger a request to the sender.
lenses.ambitious: Every dossier, including flex workers', gets a nightly completeness score, so audits (Inspectorate SZW, client audits on food safety) are passed without a scramble.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses renaming scans. What is left is handling unclear cases and sensitive files such as grievances with care.
lenses.options: For each unclear document the system offers the two or three likely employee and document-type matches, and the administrator picks one.
lenses.altitude: The administrator maintains the list of document types, the required fields and the completeness rules, and reviews a weekly sample of auto-filed documents.
reach: Certificate registration for L&D (forklift, VCA)
Dossier completeness reporting for People Analytics

tasks.human_edge: Judging sensitive documents (grievances, performance issues) and who may see them, and sorting out messy or contradictory paperwork with a site manager.
tasks.pattern_why: Unstructured scans and emails are turned into a structured, checkable record (type, employee, dates, fields) inside a fixed filing workflow. Validation against AFAS catches mismatches.

in_practice.trigger: Document lands in the HR shared mailbox, the upload form or a scan folder
steps: Extract text and classify the document type
Match it to an employee or flex worker by name, personnel number and date of birth
Extract the required fields and validate them against AFAS master data
File complete, high-confidence documents in the AFAS dossier and queue the rest for review
Send a templated request for missing signatures or pages
in_practice.human_gate: Low-confidence matches, all grievance, appraisal and medical-adjacent documents, and any field that changes pay or contract terms are approved by the administrator
systems: Power Automate with AI Builder or Azure AI Document Intelligence
data_needed: Document type list with required fields
in_practice.logs_to: Processing log in SharePoint list plus AFAS dossier history

evidence.claim: AI Builder document processing in Power Automate extracts fields from forms and PDFs
AFAS Profit exposes connectors to create and update dossier items
Classification of HR documents with an LLM reaches usable accuracy for routing

risks: Misfiled document puts personal data in the wrong dossier (AVG data breach)
Medical information slips into the dossier, which the AVG forbids for absence
Works council consent needed if the flow changes how employee data is processed
research_questions: What share of the last 3 months' incoming documents are of the ten most common types?
How accurate is employee matching on scanned site-office paperwork in a 200-document test?
Does the OR consider this a change requiring consent under WOR art. 27?

tasks.short: Enter employee changes in AFAS: addresses, hours, absences, terminations and reasons, manager performance notes.

today.trigger: Email or form from an employee or manager, sick report by phone, or a leaver notice
steps: Read the email or form and look up the employee in AFAS Profit
Type the change into the right AFAS screen
Check effective date and payroll impact
Confirm to employee or manager
Note it for payroll if it affects this month
drudgery: Retyping address changes and bank details
Entering termination reasons from free-text emails
Double entry in Excel tracking lists
today.time_sinks: Incomplete requests needing a follow-up, and changes that arrive just before the payroll cut-off.

lenses.faster: Employees and managers submit changes in AFAS InSite forms with built-in validation, so the administrator stops retyping and only handles rejects.
lenses.autonomous: Address and contact changes go straight into AFAS after validation. Termination and hours changes go through a workflow to the manager and then to payroll automatically.
lenses.ambitious: Termination reasons are captured in a fixed list for every leaver, including flex workers, so 90-day retention analysis in Power BI finally has reliable reasons.
lenses.joy: Typing addresses goes away. The administrator keeps the cases where something is odd.
lenses.options: For free-text exit emails, the system proposes the most likely termination reason codes for the manager to confirm.
lenses.altitude: The administrator designs the forms, validation rules and reason-code lists, and watches a daily exceptions report.
reach: Payroll mutation pre-check before month close
Exit reason data quality for People Analytics

tasks.human_edge: Spotting when a change looks wrong (bank account changed just before payday, a termination that does not match what the HRBP said) and handling sensitive leaver situations.
tasks.pattern_why: The inputs can be structured forms, the rules can be written down, and the result is checkable in AFAS. No model is needed at run time apart from optional reason-code suggestions.

in_practice.trigger: Employee or manager submits an AFAS InSite form
steps: Validate fields (postcode format, IBAN check, effective date, payroll cut-off)
Route to the manager for approval where the change affects contract or pay
Write the approved change to AFAS Profit
Flag payroll-relevant changes to the Payroll Specialist's month list
Send confirmation to the requester
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator handles validation failures, bank account changes (verified by callback) and terminations
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS workflow history and mutation log

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit InSite offers employee self-service forms with workflows for personal data changes
Self-service for address and bank changes removes most manual HR data entry

risks: Bank account change fraud via a compromised account
Warehouse staff without easy access to InSite on the floor
Production or performance figures from operations systems are not in AFAS and stay manual
research_questions: How many mutations per month by type, and which share could be self-service?
What share of warehouse staff use AFAS InSite or the Pocket app today?
Where do production figures live, and does anyone in HR actually need them recorded?

tasks.short: Process hires, leavers, leave, transfers and promotions in AFAS, with contract letters from SharePoint templates.

today.trigger: Manager or HRBP email that a person is hired, leaving, moving site, going on leave or being promoted
steps: Collect the details from the email and ask for what is missing
Check the CAO scale, hours and contract type
Enter the mutation in AFAS Profit
Draft the contract, addendum or letter from the SharePoint template in Word
Send for signature and file the signed copy
drudgery: Copying details from email to AFAS to Word
Checking the CAO salary table by hand
Chasing signatures
today.time_sinks: Missing details from managers, checking the ketenregeling and scale rules, and correcting letters.

lenses.faster: An agent turns the approved request into a pre-filled AFAS mutation and a draft letter from the right template, with CAO scale and chain-rule checks done.
lenses.autonomous: A manager's approved request in AFAS or an accepted offer in Recruitee starts the flow. Nothing waits for the administrator to notice an email.
lenses.ambitious: Every change is processed before its effective date, every letter is correct the first time, and payroll never gets a late mutation.
lenses.joy: No more copy-paste between three screens. The administrator checks and signs off.
lenses.options: For transfers and promotions the agent shows the scale and step options under the CAO with the pay effect of each.
lenses.altitude: The administrator maintains the templates, the CAO rule tables and the checklist per event type, and reviews error rates monthly.
reach: Payroll Specialist pre-checks of mutations
HRBP contract history checks

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what to do when a request breaks a CAO rule or the chain rule, and talking with the manager about it.
tasks.pattern_why: Several steps across AFAS, templates and approvals, with exceptions (missing info, rule conflicts). A person must approve before a contract or pay change counts.

in_practice.trigger: Approved request in AFAS workflow or offer accepted in Recruitee
steps: Pull details from the request and the AFAS record and list what is missing
Check CAO scale, hours, contract type and chain-rule history
Prepare the AFAS mutation and the letter from the SharePoint template
Send to the administrator for approval, then for signature
File the signed document and notify payroll
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator approves every mutation and letter before it is written or sent
data_needed: CAO salary tables for both CAOs
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS workflow history and an approval log in SharePoint

evidence.claim: Recruitee has an API and webhooks for candidate and offer events
AFAS Profit workflows can route HR mutations for approval
An LLM agent can draft letters from templates and check rule tables reliably with a person approving

risks: Outdated CAO tables give wrong pay in letters
Approving too fast turns the gate into a rubber stamp
Template merge errors in legal documents
research_questions: How many mutations per month per event type, and how many need correcting today?
Can the CAO tables be kept as one maintained data source?
Which AFAS connectors are licensed and allowed by the AFAS partner?

tasks.short: Screen applications in Recruitee for hard requirements: right to work, driving licence, certificates, availability.

today.trigger: New applications arrive in Recruitee for a vacancy
steps: Open each CV and answers to screening questions
Check hard requirements (C/CE licence, code 95, forklift certificate, right to work, shift availability)
Move candidates to the next stage or flag for the Recruiter
Ask for missing documents
drudgery: Opening hundreds of CVs for warehouse roles
Looking for the same few facts in different CV formats
Sending the same document requests
today.time_sinks: High volumes for warehouse and seasonal roles, CVs in different languages, and missing information.

lenses.faster: Each application gets a one-screen summary of hard requirements met, missing or unclear, with the source sentence quoted, so the check takes seconds.
lenses.autonomous: A missing document or answer triggers a polite request to the candidate in their language. Nothing is rejected without a person.
lenses.ambitious: Every applicant gets a response within two working days, including those for seasonal peaks, which helps time to hire and offer acceptance.
lenses.joy: Hunting for the licence code in a CV goes away. What is left is talking to borderline candidates.
lenses.options: For borderline candidates it suggests alternative open roles at another site or shift that fit better.
lenses.altitude: The administrator and Recruiter define knock-out criteria per vacancy and audit the summaries and outcomes for bias each quarter.
reach: Recruiter first-round screening
Pre-checks of agency flex candidates

tasks.human_edge: The decision to advance or reject stays human, as does fairness judgement on gaps, foreign qualifications and unusual careers.
tasks.pattern_why: Under the EU AI Act, AI used to evaluate candidates is high-risk (Annex III). Keeping the person as decision-maker, with AI summarising only verifiable hard requirements, limits risk and keeps accountability clear.

steps: Extract hard-requirement facts from CV and screening answers
Show met, missing or unclear per requirement with quoted evidence
Draft a request for missing information for the administrator to send
Administrator moves the candidate to a stage
in_practice.human_gate: Every stage move and every rejection is done by a person
systems: LLM service under a data processing agreement
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee candidate notes and an audit log of AI summaries

evidence.claim: EU AI Act classifies AI for recruitment and candidate evaluation as high-risk
LLMs can extract licence and certificate facts from CVs with quoted evidence

risks: Bias against candidates with non-standard CVs
EU AI Act duties (transparency, human oversight, logging) if the summary drives decisions
Candidates not told AI is used, breaching AVG transparency
research_questions: How many applications per month per vacancy type, and how long does a check take today?
Does Recruitee offer built-in AI screening, and is it acceptable to the OR and the DPO?
In a blind test of 100 CVs, how often does the summary miss or invent a requirement?

tasks.short: Answer staff questions on pay, CAO, leave, benefits, eligibility and mandatory training by mail, Teams and phone.

today.trigger: Employee or manager asks by email, Teams, phone or at the desk
steps: Read the question and work out which CAO or policy applies
Look it up in SharePoint, the CAO text or AFAS
Write or say the answer
Pass it on to payroll or an HRBP when needed
drudgery: The same questions about holiday hours, ADV and shift allowances again and again
Looking up CAO articles
Explaining in English to flex workers
today.time_sinks: Repeat questions, two CAOs with different rules, and language barriers with Polish and Romanian staff.

lenses.faster: A Teams HR assistant answers general policy and CAO questions with a citation to the source article, and drafts replies to the rest for the administrator.
lenses.autonomous: General questions are answered at once, day or night shift. Personal questions about own salary or exceptions go to the administrator with a draft attached.
lenses.ambitious: Every warehouse worker and flex worker can ask in their own language and get a correct, sourced answer, which may cut avoidable pay disputes and absence confusion.
lenses.joy: Answering the hundredth holiday-hours question goes away. The administrator keeps the questions where a person needs help.
lenses.options: For questions with a choice (unpaid leave or holiday hours, parental leave timing), it lays out the options and their effects.
lenses.altitude: The administrator owns the knowledge base: keeps policies current, reviews unanswered and wrongly answered questions weekly, and adds answers.
reach: First-line payslip questions for the Payroll Specialist
Benefit explanations for the Compensation and Benefits Specialist

tasks.human_edge: Personal and sensitive situations (illness, conflict, money trouble) where trust and discretion matter, and the judgement on exceptions.
tasks.pattern_why: The bot can answer general questions grounded in sources, but anything personal or touching pay needs a person to approve before it is sent.

in_practice.trigger: Question in a Teams chat or to the HR mailbox
steps: Classify as general policy, personal or sensitive
Answer general questions from SharePoint policies and CAO texts with citations
For personal questions, look up the AFAS record and draft an answer for the administrator
Route sensitive topics (illness, grievance) straight to a person
Log unanswered questions for knowledge base updates
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator approves every answer that uses personal data or pay figures
in_practice.logs_to: Copilot Studio conversation analytics and an HR ticket list

evidence.claim: Copilot Studio builds Teams agents grounded on SharePoint content
Policy chatbots deflect a large share of repeat HR questions

risks: Wrong answer about pay or leave rights creates a claim
Outdated policy documents in SharePoint
Works council consent may be needed; employees may fear monitoring
research_questions: What share of questions over two weeks are general rather than personal?
Are both CAO texts and the policies current and in one place?
Will the OR agree, and on what terms for logging conversations?

tasks.short: Do the paperwork from accepted offer to first day: contract, ID/WAV check, loonheffingen, accounts, training.

steps: Request personal data, ID, bank details and loonheffingen form from the new hire
Check ID and right to work (WAV) and keep the copy as required
Create the employee in AFAS and draft the contract
Request VOG where needed, IT account, PPE and Studytube enrolments
Send the welcome and first-day information
drudgery: Re-entering candidate data from Recruitee into AFAS
Emailing IT, the site and L&D separately
Chasing documents from new hires
today.time_sinks: Missing documents, start dates a few days away during the season, and coordinating three sites.

lenses.faster: An accepted offer in Recruitee triggers a checklist that pre-fills AFAS, drafts the contract and sends the requests to IT, the site and Studytube in one go.
lenses.autonomous: Document requests and reminders to the new hire run on their own, and the checklist shows status to the hiring manager.
lenses.ambitious: Every new hire, including seasonal ones, is fully set up before day one, which supports onboarding completed in week one and 90-day retention.
lenses.joy: Retyping and chasing go away. The administrator gets more time for the welcome call and day-one questions.
lenses.options: For tight start dates it shows which steps can run in parallel and which block the start.
lenses.altitude: The administrator owns the onboarding checklist per role and site and watches a dashboard of new hires at risk of not being ready.
reach: Studytube enrolments for mandatory certificates (L&D)
Payroll set-up checks

tasks.human_edge: The legal ID and right-to-work check, which must be done with the original document, and the personal welcome that shapes the first 90 days.
tasks.pattern_why: Many steps across systems with exceptions. The contract and the ID/WAV check need a person's sign-off.

steps: Create the new hire in AFAS from Recruitee data
Draft the contract from the right template and CAO scale
Send the new hire a secure upload request for documents and track reminders
Raise IT, site and Studytube requests
Show readiness status to the administrator and manager
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator checks the ID and right to work in person and approves the contract before signature
data_needed: Onboarding checklist per role and site
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS onboarding workflow and checklist status in SharePoint

evidence.claim: Recruitee to AFAS data transfer of hires can be automated

risks: ID copies stored too long or too widely (AVG)
A missed WAV check brings fines from the Labour Inspectorate
Studytube integration may be limited
research_questions: How long does offer to ready-to-start take today, and where does it stall?
Is there an existing Recruitee to AFAS integration in use?
Can Studytube enrolments be created through an API?

tasks.short: Look up employee files to answer questions and prepare data for contract renewals and personnel decisions.

today.trigger: HRBP, manager or payroll asks for information about an employee or group
steps: Search the AFAS record and dossier
Read contracts, addenda and absence history
Put together the answer or overview in Excel or email
Check for dates such as contract end and notice
drudgery: Scrolling through dossiers for one date
Building the same contract-end lists by hand
Counting contracts for the chain rule
today.time_sinks: Old dossiers with scans, information spread over AFAS and SharePoint, and urgent requests.

lenses.faster: A question in plain language gives a sourced summary of the file, and fixed checks such as the chain rule and the aanzegplicht date are computed automatically.
lenses.autonomous: Every month a list of contracts ending in the next 2 months, with chain-rule status and the aanzegplicht deadline, goes to each manager and HRBP without being asked.
lenses.ambitious: No contract is ever renewed by accident or ended without timely notice, which avoids the aanzegvergoeding and unwanted permanent contracts.
lenses.joy: Digging through scans goes away. What is left is advising the HRBP on what the file means.
lenses.options: For a renewal it shows the options (renew fixed-term, permanent, end) with the legal effect of each.
lenses.altitude: The administrator maintains the contract-history data and the rules, and checks a sample of generated summaries.
reach: Preparing personnel cases for HRBPs
Data requests from People Analytics

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what may be shared with whom (need to know under the AVG) and spotting what is missing or odd in a file.
tasks.pattern_why: Reading and summarising unstructured dossiers into a checkable answer with citations, inside a workflow with access control. Date rules run as plain code.

in_practice.trigger: Request from an HRBP or manager, or the monthly contract-end run
steps: Check that the requester is allowed to see the requested data
Retrieve the AFAS record and dossier documents
Compute the chain rule and aanzegplicht dates with fixed rules
Summarise with citations to source documents
Administrator reviews and sends
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator reviews each summary before it is sent
systems: Copilot or LLM service under a data processing agreement
in_practice.logs_to: Request log with requester, purpose and data shared

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot can summarise documents a user has access to in SharePoint
Chain-rule and notice-date checks can be written as fixed rules on AFAS data

risks: Oversharing personal data beyond need to know
Wrong date logic where the CAO deviates from the chain rule
Incomplete scanned history gives a false chain-rule count
research_questions: How many file requests per week, and of what types?
Does the CAO deviate from the standard chain rule, and is contract history complete in AFAS?
Is Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed and are dossier permissions set correctly?

tasks.short: Chase managers, employees and agencies for missing documents: signed contracts, certificates, forms, flex worker papers.

today.trigger: Missing-document list, audit or a contract or certificate deadline
steps: Check which documents are missing per employee
Email or call managers, employees or agencies
Track replies in Excel
Remind again and escalate
File what comes in
drudgery: Writing the same reminder emails
Updating the tracking spreadsheet
Logging into three agency portals
today.time_sinks: Slow site managers, shift workers who do not read email, and agencies sending documents in different formats.

lenses.faster: Missing items are detected from the dossier rules, and reminders go out with a personal upload link, so the tracking spreadsheet disappears.
lenses.autonomous: Reminders run on a schedule by Teams, email or SMS for shift workers and escalate to the site manager after two misses.
lenses.ambitious: Every flex worker from the three agencies has a complete file before their first shift, including certificates, which cuts audit and safety risk.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the spreadsheet or the tenth reminder. What is left is the phone call that actually unblocks it.
lenses.options: For each overdue item the system suggests the best channel and person to chase, based on what worked before.
lenses.altitude: The administrator sets the required-document rules and escalation paths and reviews the overdue dashboard weekly.
reach: Agency document checks with the Bookkeepers
Certificate expiry follow-up for L&D

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which manager to call, when to push and when to give leeway, and sorting out agency disputes.
tasks.pattern_why: Several steps across channels with exceptions. Reminders can run on their own, but escalations and acceptance of documents need a person.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly completeness check finds a missing or expiring document
steps: List missing items per employee, manager and agency
Send reminders with a secure upload link through the right channel
Check incoming documents and file them
Escalate after the set number of reminders
Update the overdue dashboard
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator handles escalations and accepts documents that fail automatic checks
data_needed: Required documents per role and worker type
in_practice.logs_to: Reminder and escalation log in SharePoint, and a Power BI overdue view

evidence.claim: Power Automate can send scheduled reminders and collect files
Studytube tracks certificate completion and expiry

risks: Reminder fatigue makes managers ignore messages
Agency portals may not offer exports or APIs
Sending personal data by SMS or insecure links
research_questions: How many documents are open at any time, by type and source?
Do the three agency portals offer exports or APIs?
Which channel do shift workers actually respond to?
